doc.title: Mike Davis interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, April 1, 2024

title: Aerosmith session with David Campbell
summary: Rowe reads a list of artists; Davis describes a chaotic Aerosmith horn session saved by arranger David Campbell.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Session players on the hits: "I played on that record"

blocks.x: Okay I’m going to try a little something on you here. I have a list of some of the people that you’ve recorded for or perhaps done a tour with. And I’m going to start reading it and I want you to stop me if there’s something of significance that you’d like to say about it. All right?
Okay I mean I can say something about all of these —
I bet you can. Yeah we’ve got six hours here so let’s get started.
The Aerosmith session, I just recorded one record for them and it was a kind of a larger horn section. I think there was two trombones on it and two or three trumpets, maybe

three saxophones. And I just remember — oh what’s his last name — David Campbell who is the pop singer Beck who was a big star, still is I guess, Beck, who I played with on some other things but Beck, his dad is a really good arranger and he was kind of known as the arranger for the rock bands. He did some stuff for the Stones, he’s done lots of different folks. He was the arranger on it and thank goodness because it was party central in the booth. I mean it sounded like a pet shop burning down whenever they would come on and try to ask us to do something. And there was no way you were — like your question was going to get answered if it weren’t for David. So that session was very, like it was chaotic but at the same time a lot of fun and memorable for sure.
